title: Network Participation Agreements: Overpayment Notices, Lookback and Recovery Entries
content:
This is the Payment Integrity standard for overpayments under the **Network Participation Agreements**.

## When an overpayment arises

An overpayment arises when a member claim paid to the practice is reprocessed to a lower payment, or when an orthodontic payment is reversed. A claim may be reprocessed, for example, after a coordination-of-benefits correction, after an eligibility back-out following a lapse, or because it was a duplicate.

The overpaid amount is the original payment less the corrected payment.

## Lookback for issuing the notice

An overpayment notice may be issued only within the overpayment lookback after the original payment date of the overpaid claim.

| Element | Basis |
|---|---|
| Clock starts | The original payment date: the adjudicated date of the source dental line or vision service, or the payment date of the source orthodontic payment, as Cascade's claim records show it |
| Length | The agreement type's lookback, in calendar days (365 under the savings network agreement, 545 under every other type) |
| Comparison | The notice must be dated no later than the last day of the lookback. A notice dated on the last day is in time. |
| Fraud | Overpayments arising from fraud are not limited, because every agreement type carries the fraud exception |

**Boundary (hypothetical).** Under a 545-day lookback, a notice dated on the 545th calendar day after the original payment date is in time. A notice dated on the 546th day is not, unless the overpayment arose from fraud.

## Amounts not pursued

Overpayments below the agreement type's minimum recovery amount are not pursued.

## Refund window and start of offsets

**Clause on the refund window.** This clause is **no longer in force** and is superseded by the current basis: *The practice may refund within the refund window of calendar days after the notice; an overpayment may be offset against a remittance only after the refund window following the overpayment notice has passed and while no dispute of it is pending.*

**Clause on the start of offsets.** This clause is **no longer in force** and is superseded by the current basis: *The offset may start on the day after the notice date plus the refund window of calendar days.*

The refund window figure itself stays valid: 45 calendar days under every agreement type.

## Recovery entries

The ledger records four kinds of entry for an overpayment:

- the overpayment notice, which adds the overpaid amount to the receivable;
- a withholding, where the amount is offset against a later remittance;
- a refund received from the practice;
- a reduction, where the overpayment is reduced or withdrawn after a dispute, or written off below the recovery minimum.

Each recovery references the overpayment it settles, and recoveries never exceed the open amount.

**Open amount of an overpayment.** This is the amount on its notice, less the total of every withholding, refund received and reduction that references it. It is counted over the life of that overpayment case.

**Hypothetical.** A notice for 300.00 USD has one withholding of 120.00 USD and one refund received of 50.00 USD against it. Its open amount is 130.00 USD, and no further recovery against it may exceed 130.00 USD.

superseded_clauses: The practice may refund within overpayment_refund_window_days calendar days after the notice; an overpayment may be offset against a remittance only after the refund window following the overpayment notice has passed and while no dispute of it is pending.
The offset may start on the day after the notice date plus overpayment_refund_window_days calendar days.
